regenerable_on: a lab guest carrying a virtio-scsi disk and a QEMU NVMe controller, each given a serial and a wwn in its domain definition. The default guest has neither — its disks are virtio-blk, which appear in no hardware walk — so a re-stage on a plain guest reproduces the qemu-guest variant instead and this one silently vanishes from a drift diff. test/vm-lab stages the two devices; the values below are the scrubbed ones, not the planted ones.
note: The first hardware capture with a real disk in it, and the variant R3c's first acceptance item is judged on: one disk reachable from its by-id spelling, its kernel name and its WWN — one object, one page, every name on it. qemu-guest could not teach it, because a virtio-blk disk appears in neither the scsi nor the nvme walk, so that capture held two ata_piix hosts and nothing behind them. It cost four things on the way in, each recorded where it was found: the scrub manifest grew the three identity attributes it had promised would refuse; the binary seam (SCSI VPD page 0x80) got a primitive on both implementations, having been an inline read that would have published the serial of whichever machine replayed; the scrubber and the detectors each learned to fold base64 and ASCII-hex, because an identifier written in an encoding was invisible to both; and the wwn pass was found substituting its own replacement a second time, reachable only through a prefix ending in a non-word character, which `naa.` is and `wwn-0x` is not. Extended the same day to carry the VERB surface: the capture now runs the reference's object and evidence paths for every scsi, nvme and platform object beside the collection walk, so the corpus can replay a verb request instead of the collector's verb tests staging a fixture of what their author believes sysfs looks like. That found two more unseamed reads — _read raised UnicodeDecodeError on a binary attribute, which is how every evidence request for a SCSI disk had been failing unnoticed, and the directory probe used os.path.isdir, which under replay asked the machine doing the replaying — and it found the DMI identity the platform exemption promised this collector never read.
coverage_note: What this guest still cannot teach. There is no SAS expander and no SES enclosure, so sas_address, the enclosure slot tree and SlotStatus are reached by nothing here and stay unclassified in the scrub manifest — the walk's deny-by-default refusal is the gate that forces them to be written down when a capture from a host with a shelf arrives. There is no smartctl snapshot and no udisks2 on the bus, so every SMART depth is absent and both drives carry SmartUnobservable rather than a health reading — which is the discipline this collection exists to hold, asserted below rather than assumed. The PCIe link is a QEMU one lane at 2.5 GT/s and the bridge above publishes no maximum, so the link rules are not fired by this variant either. The verb capture covers scsi, nvme and platform only: pci and usb would add the whole attribute set of every function and hub on the machine, which is payload weight for a surface those two answer identically to each other. So an `object pci …` request refuses under replay rather than declining, and this variant makes no claim about it.
anchors_note: Transcribed by hand from the scrubbed payloads, each naming the file and the member it came from. The scsi disk: read.json's /sys/bus/scsi/devices/0:0:0:0 gives type 0 (the kernel's code for a disk, which DeviceType names), state and wwid; the serial is read-bytes.json's vpd_pg80, base64 of SCSI VPD page 0x80, past its four header octets; the by-id spellings are udev.json's DEVLINKS for /sys/block/sda, filtered to that directory, and the wwn family carries the sysfs wwid beside udev's wwn-… link because they are two spellings of one identity. Devices 1 on host0 is the child count of the walk. SmartTemperatureC absent on the disk is the point of the coverage note: hwmon's one sensor is the NVMe controller's, and 49850 millidegrees is 49.85 degrees, which lands on 49.8 rather than 49.9 because both implementations round half to EVEN — Python's rule, reproduced in Go as math.RoundToEven, and the half-way case is exactly the one a hand-transcribed anchor gets wrong. The NVMe controller: serial and state from /sys/class/nvme/nvme0, wwid from the namespace's own block attribute (a wwid belongs to a namespace), and the link facts from /sys/class/nvme/nvme0/device — one lane at 2.5 GT/s, which the PCIe table converts to 250 MB/s each way. commit_objects 4 is host0, host1, host2 and the one disk.
